selected_evidence.summary: useradd creates opsadmin (uid 1000); authorized_keys populated with exactly the required ed25519 key with correct ownership/permissions

selected_evidence.requirement: SSH requires key-based authentication (password auth disabled)
selected_evidence.summary: sshd_config.d/99-key-only.conf written and passes sshd -t; effective config (sshd -T) shows pubkeyauthentication yes / passwordauthentication no / permitemptypasswords no; live SSH attempt restricted to password auth is rejected with 'Permission denied (publickey)'

selected_evidence.requirement: Key-based SSH login actually functions for opsadmin
selected_evidence.summary: SSH login using a temporary ed25519 key added to authorized_keys succeeds (whoami=opsadmin, LOGIN_OK), proving the pubkey auth path works end-to-end; temp key was removed afterward leaving only the required key (cmd-2473e1a7cf284871)
Captured boot_id 4d70780a-0bff-4d50-8c53-62faa1ccc945, ssh.service active, key-only sshd policy, opsadmin user and authorized_keys all healthy prior to restart
`sudo reboot` issued via backgrounded nohup; command returned 'reboot issued, pid 1848' immediately
